source_context_translations.translation: The Way is empty, yet when used it is never filled up. Deep and still, it seems like the source of all things. It blunts its sharpness, unties its knots, softens its light, and shares its dust. Deep and still, it seems as if it might endure.
I do not know whose child it is; it seems to be before the Lord on High.
Heaven and earth are not humane; they treat the myriad things as straw dogs;
The sage is not humane; he treats the people as straw dogs.
Between heaven and earth, is it not like a bellows?
Empty, yet never exhausted; the more it moves, the more comes forth.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates that something happens on some occasions but not always.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Marks intermittent occurrence rather than uncertainty.
Sentence Translations (English): Human life is sometimes long and sometimes short.
Sometimes it rains, sometimes it is clear; the seasons are not fixed.
In war, one may win or lose; nothing is certain.
There may be unusual trees by the roadside.
Sentences: 兵者或勝或敗，未可必也。

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates possibility or uncertainty: something may happen, may be the case, or may be one among alternatives.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often has a speculative or open-ended force rather than firm assertion.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having no empty space left; completely filled.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes a resulting state rather than the act of filling.
Sentence Translations (English): When a vessel is full, it is overflowing.
When the granaries are full, the people are then secure.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To become or make full, with nothing more able to be contained.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it suggests complete saturation or exhaustion of capacity.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A deep body of water or deep hollow space.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concrete physical depth, not figurative profundity.
Sentence Translations (English): The river has a deep abyss.
He threw a stone into the deep.
He stood by the edge of the abyss.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Describes great depth, literally or figuratively, especially as something hidden, far down, or profoundly still.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it evokes unfathomable depth and hidden source-power.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A sentence-final or phrase-final particle used to give an exclamatory, evocative, or rhythmic force, without adding propositional meaning.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Adds cadence and a contemplative tone rather than factual content.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; especially literary and received early philosophical prose

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Used as a comparative marker to state resemblance between two things.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A more explicit comparison than the verbal sense.
Sentence Translations (English): The sound is like wind and rain.
Its form is like a crane.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a comparison indicating resemblance or appearance, often with a tentative or as-if quality.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests likeness without identity, and often leaves the comparison deliberately open.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A forebear from whom a family or line descends.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Human lineage rather than abstract source.
Sentence Translations (English): He does not forget his ancestors.
The ancestor is in the elder generation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): That from which something comes forth or is derived; an original source or root.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it points to primal origin, not a human ancestor.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To check, subdue, or weaken a person's resolve, strength, or momentum.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Applies to force or spirit, not physical edges.
Sentence Translations (English): The crowd's talk crushed his resolve.
The army's sharp momentum was checked.
Though repeatedly defeated, he was not discouraged.
Its keen spirit has already been blunted.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To reduce sharpness, edge, or force; to dull or weaken something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here the action is one of softening aggressive sharpness.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The pointed or cutting part of a tool, weapon, or object.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concrete physical sharpness rather than figurative acuity.
Sentence Translations (English): The arrowhead is sharp as new.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having a fine point or edge; by extension, acute or forceful in quality.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage the sense is of an edge or intensity that can be softened.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To make something clear by giving an interpretation or account.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): An intellectual clarification, distinct from physical untying.
Sentence Translations (English): I will explain it for you.
The doubts have already been resolved.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To undo binding, separation, or entanglement; to release or resolve what is knotted or fastened.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means removing constriction or entanglement, not explanation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having many scattered parts, or being variously intermingled.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes a state of multiplicity or dispersion, not necessarily trouble.
Sentence Translations (English): The grasses and trees were densely mixed.
Carriages and horses arrived in crowds.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A tangled, mixed-up, or disordered condition; something that is knotted, perplexing, or hard to separate.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests both literal tangling and disorder of things or affairs.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Splendor, honor, or shining prestige; by extension, a brilliant quality.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often more social or moral than purely physical light.
Sentence Translations (English): His virtue shone through the four seas.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Visible brightness or radiance emitted or reflected by something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it refers to outward brilliance or brilliance that can be subdued and harmonized.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The ordinary, dusty business of the human world, especially what is common, mundane, or distracting.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A metaphorical extension from dust to mundane existence.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary and philosophical usage
Sentence Translations (English): He lived long amid the dust of the world.
His mind is far from worldly matters.
He is not stained by worldly burdens.
He has temporarily left worldly affairs.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Fine dry particles of earth or matter; by extension, the ordinary world or triviality.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it contrasts with light and suggests common, low, or worldly obscurity.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Covered with water or deeply saturated with liquid.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A physical state of being soaked or immersed.
Sentence Translations (English): The clothes were soaked by the rain.
The ground was damp and wet.
The boat was immersed in the water.
His lower garments were all soaked.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Describes a deep, settled, obscure stillness or hidden fullness, often of water or of an inward state.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests quiet depth rather than motion or brightness.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To hold something in being, keep it safe, or maintain it unchanged.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Focused on active maintenance rather than mere continued existence.
Sentence Translations (English): Good governance can preserve the people.
He left writings to preserve his meaning.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To continue to be present, survive, or persist rather than disappear.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means a state of lingering presence, not preservation by effort.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): First-person singular pronoun used by the speaker to refer to himself.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Plain self-reference with no marked humility or emphasis.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Interrogative pronoun asking to whom something belongs or is related.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Marks possession or lineage in a question.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Interrogative pronoun asking for a person’s identity or source.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often broad in scope: who, which person, or whose, depending on structure.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): An honorific used for respected men, especially thinkers, teachers, or gentlemen.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Marks respect and social status, not family relation.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; common literary and philosophical usage
Sentence Translations (English): I wish to follow you, Master.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A male child, or more generally a child or descendant.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it denotes offspring or a filial descendant, not the honorific use.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The animal elephant.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): The concrete animal sense, distinct from resemblance.
Sentence Translations (English): There are elephants in the south.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To take the form or appearance of something else, or to be analogous to it.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is analogical, pointing to likeness rather than identity.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A human sovereign ruling an empire.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): The political, human-ruler sense.
Sentence Translations (English): The emperor ruled over the myriad states.
The emperor departed from the capital.
The ministers obeyed the emperor's command.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A highest divine ruler or sovereign heavenly power.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this context it refers to the highest divine being or cosmic sovereign, not a human emperor.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A forefather or predecessor in a family line.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used substantively for predecessors in lineage or antiquity.
Sentence Translations (English): He sacrificed to the ancestors in the ancestral temple.
He inherited the intentions of his predecessors.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates that one thing comes earlier in time, order, or rank than another.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it marks primordial precedence, not spatial frontness.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Showing compassion or goodwill toward others; humane.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes a personal quality or attitude.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; common literary and philosophical usage
Sentence Translations (English): The ruler's heart is not benevolent.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A moral disposition of compassionate regard for others, especially as an ethical virtue.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here negated, it means not acting from conventional moral favoritism or sentiment.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Ritual straw effigies used temporarily in sacrifice and then discarded.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Denotes something treated ceremonially but without lasting attachment or favoritism.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The broad mass of ordinary subjects or civilians in a society.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A collective political-social term, not a list of surnames in this context.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): An intervening space or time between things.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Focuses on separation or elapsed space/time.
Sentence Translations (English): There is a valley between the two mountains.
The space between the rooms is very narrow.
There is nothing happening in between.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates the space, interval, or relationship separating two things, or the region in which they lie.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it denotes the space lying between heaven and earth.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates continuation or persistence of a state.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Emphasizes persistence over time.
Sentence Translations (English): Though old, he is still vigorous.
The rain has not yet stopped.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks comparison or approximation, suggesting resemblance rather than identity.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often introduces a simile or analogy with a tentative, rhetorical tone.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A device for blowing air, especially to stoke fire or drive air through a channel.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The paired image stresses a hollowed, working emptiness that produces movement or breath.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A particle used to express wonder, emphasis, or rhetorical emphasis.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Marks exclamation rather than interrogation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A sentence-final particle used to form questions or rhetorical questions.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often softens the question and can carry rhetorical or contemplative force.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary and philosophical prose

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To bend the body or a thing, or to submit and give way.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A physical or figurative yielding, distinct from exhaustion.
Sentence Translations (English): He does not yield his will.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To become used up, drained, or no longer constricted or limited in capacity.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means the opposite of being squeezed or emptied of capacity: the inner void is not exhausted.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Physical movement or stirring as a state or event.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Names the state of moving rather than the action of moving.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To begin motion, to carry out an action, or to stir from a state of rest.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it contrasts with emptiness by suggesting active functioning and circulation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To become better after illness, injury, or damage.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A medical or restorative sense, distinct from degree adverbial use.
Sentence Translations (English): After a long time, he became increasingly calm.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates a rising degree or a progressive increase beyond what came before.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks intensification over time or under pressure.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in the Wang Bi recension
